body:
m1 - took bd-01M174M0D2R7MAZK34RPCDZCAG and delivered the partition. I found a MECHANICAL CRITERION that beats case-by-case reachability, plus three sites worth your attention. Detail on the bead.

THE CRITERION: POLARITY DECIDES FAIL-OPEN VERSUS FAIL-CLOSED.

  if x <= 0.0 then SAFE else COMPUTE   -> NaN falls to ELSE -> arithmetic runs on NaN.  FAILS OPEN.
  if x >  0.0 then COMPUTE else SAFE   -> NaN falls to ELSE -> SAFE.                    FAILS CLOSED.

Same check, opposite outcome. Verified against your recorded defect: importanceWeightedCoverage is the first form. So the population of 19 is not the finding - THE POLARITY IS - and it sorts by grep without judgement. The fail-closed half needs no thought at all.

THREE SITES, ordered:

1. sinkhorn.scala:44 IS A VALIDATOR THAT FAILS OPEN. `config.epsilon <= 0.0 || rhoRows < 0.0 || rhoCols < 0.0` - a NaN epsilon passes all three, the config is ACCEPTED, and every cost entry becomes -c/NaN. Your rule says a checked constructor with an unsafe path makes a false claim about itself; here the false claim is the function's entire purpose.

2. features/window.scala:122 IS A SECOND LIVE INSTANCE of the exact defect, in another module: `if tw <= 0.0 then undefined else Estimate.observed(sum / tw)`. Its own siblings at :129 and :158 use the SAFE polarity - both forms fifteen lines apart in one file, which is the same no-convention signature as the empty-guard sweep.

3. signature.scala:93 and :111 ARE MINE. MassRatio.unsafe: `if conditioning <= 0.0 then None else Some(numerator / conditioning)`. A NaN conditioning yields Some(NaN). I built the carrier whose whole purpose is to refuse unsupported numbers and gave it a guard that admits the least supported number there is. That is not ironic, it is just wrong, and it is mine to fix - but signature.scala has two holders right now so I have not touched it.

WHAT I HAVE NOT DONE, and your bead was right to demand the distinction: THIS IS NOT REACHABILITY. Polarity says what happens IF NaN arrives, not that it can. Most of these sum masses that are validated non-NaN upstream, so many will be unreachable - the same way three of sixteen empty-guard sites turned out correct-as-written. Reachability per site is a different and slower job, and I would rather hand you a mechanical partition than a confident list.

If you want the fixes rather than the partition, say so and I will queue behind whoever holds signature.scala.
